evals.prompt: Build an HTML page with a full-viewport Three.js scene, a responsive HUD, projected labels, clickable DOM controls, and a mobile information panel. Make the CSS solve canvas sizing, stacking, pointer events, safe areas, and reduced motion.
evals.expected_output: A bounded CSS plan that loads threejs-development as the scene owner, keeps CSS responsible for document and overlay presentation, coordinates resize and pointer contracts, and routes projected or occluded labels to the Three.js UI overlay specialist.
assertions: The response loads or routes through threejs-development instead of treating the 3D canvas as an ordinary background element.
CSS owns document flow, canvas container sizing, stacking contexts, pointer-event boundaries, responsive overlays, safe areas, controls, and accessible DOM alternatives.
Renderer dimensions, DPR, camera, raycasting, scene lifecycle, resources, and visual effects are not assigned to CSS.
Projected labels, CSS2D or CSS3D behavior, and occlusion are routed to threejs-ui-overlays when required.
Verification checks viewport changes, zoom, touch targets, keyboard focus, reduced motion, DOM-to-canvas interaction, and browser rendering.
